title: SBR-7: A Randomized-Seed Adversarial Pop Quiz Against a Blockchain-Interaction Stack — 6 Probes Drawn From 12 by a Publicly Committed Seed, 6/6 Held (Preregistered, With a Disclosed Authoring-Defect Amendment)
description:
SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. Not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads synthetic. No customer-identifiable data appears in this record (POL-DISC-001).

SBR-7 — a randomized-seed adversarial pop quiz against a brand-new attack surface: the program's own blockchain-interaction stack. Following SBR-6 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23445047), 6 probes were drawn from a frozen pool of 12 by a seeded PRNG, the seed (78bf5e1, the prereg commit sha) committed publicly BEFORE the draw so the exam could not be cherry-picked. Whatever drew, ran. Deterministic adjudication; no LLM in the decision path; all probes lab-local and synthetic — only 32-byte SHA-256 digests crossed any boundary (POL-DISC-001).

The draw pulled: P01 RECEIPT-SWAP (a receipt for artifact A presented as proof of artifact B: refused, digest mismatch => orphan), P03 RECOVER-ARC (drift re-anchored, superseded receipt retained in history), P05 DIGEST-ONLY-BOUNDARY (committed digest == sha256(artifact): proof no artifact bytes ever transit), P06 MERKLE-PARSE (valid proof paths), P09 REPLAY-STAMP (stamping the same content twice commits an identical digest: idempotent existence proof), P11 PQC-AUTHORITY-NON-NEGOTIABLE (the chain-proves-existence / PQC-retains-authority split held; no substitution). Result: 6/6 PASS (receipt v1.1, sha a18cf2d9...9993e823).

Disclosed (audit-and-correction doctrine): the v1.0 run scored 5/6 — the P11 probe had an authoring defect (a case-sensitive substring check against a protocol that prints the disclosure in caps; the system under test was never at fault). The v1.0 FAIL receipt is preserved in the bundle; the harness was amended v1.1 forward-only with the reason disclosed and the exam re-run clean on the same seed. This is the fifth time the preregistration discipline caught an authoring defect before it could masquerade as a result — a recurring finding about the method in its own right.

Context: this battery certifies safe blockchain interaction for the SIP-034..037 chain-of-custody stack (OpenTimestamps hash-only anchoring of the governance corpus; companion record DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23445728). The program's claim 'we can safely interact with the blockchain' now carries a randomized, seeded, receipt-backed exam. Scope caveat (load-bearing): synthetic forge, lab-local, free public calendars; not a production certification. Dual Mesh Benchmark status: NOT MEASURED in this record (no neural-mesh inference involved); program benchmark DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23321637 (DeepSeek column 10.5281/zenodo.23345241). Provenance: append-only public ledger entries 0162-0168, github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen. DCAI community: zenodo.org/communities/dcai. Two-key curation: drafted and vetted by the system (Gabriel), published on the owner's explicit GO (chat authorization, 2026-10-17 ~23:00 CT).
